Subject: Hosted API evaluation: quickstart & rate limits

Hi Olivia —

Great talking earlier today. Thanks for the time and for walking through FastStore's inference needs (mainly high throughput for search reranking + embeddings). Per our call, I wanted to summarize next steps and give you a fast path to evaluate Redwood's Hosted API:

Quick summary from the demo:
- You’re primarily evaluating latency-sensitive reranking for search (p50 target ~60–120ms),
- Embeddings for semantic search and similarity, and
- Interested in understanding when to move from Hosted -> Dedicated capacity.

Suggested next steps:
1) Try the Hosted API quickstart (no infra changes): I can provision a short-lived API key for testing, or you can self-signup here: https://app.redwood.example/signup
2) Run the sample reranking request (curl example below) and measure p50 on your dataset
3) If you hit throughput/latency limits, we can discuss Dedicated pools (reserved GPUs) or Private VPC.

Sample curl (Hosted API):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1-large","input":"Rank these search results by relevance: ...","max_tokens":64}'

Defaults and rate guidance (Hosted):
- Default token rate: 60k tokens/min tenant-burstable (applies to new evaluation accounts)
- Concurrent requests: 20 concurrent requests per API key by default
- Burst: short bursts up to 2x baseline for a few minutes; sustained higher throughput is better on Dedicated
- If you need sustained <100ms p50 at scale, Dedicated is often recommended (we can scope sizing after you run initial tests)

I’ve attached a short quickstart guide and the rate/limits doc. Marissa (cc) will help with any integration questions and can join a quick technical troubleshooting session if you want to run tests together.

If it works for you, I can provision a test key (7-day) and a sandbox workspace for FastStore — should I go ahead?

Thanks,

Thanks Olivia — great questions. Short answers up front, then details:
- 60k tokens/min is per-tenant baseline for evaluation (applies across API keys for the workspace).
- Throttling: we have per-second and per-minute enforcement; typical enforcement is a token-leaky-bucket that surfaces 429s when sustained limits are exceeded.
- SLA: Hosted tier has a best-effort availability guarantee for eval accounts; SLA-backed uptime and explicit latency targets are part of Reserved/Dedicated contracts.

Details & recommended approach:
1) Rate limits and concurrency
- Eval (Hosted) default: 60k tokens/min workspace baseline, spike tolerance ~2x for short bursts. Per-second enforcement approximates to ~1k tokens/sec smoothing but depends on request distribution.
- Concurrency: 20 concurrent requests by default. If you need higher concurrency for throughput testing, we can temporarily raise this for the sandbox.
- For sustained 2000 qps at ~160 tokens/request (~320k tokens/sec), Hosted eval won’t be the right fit — that’s squarely into Dedicated territory. We can size a Dedicated pool (N GPUs, batching) and share cost estimates once you run the correctness/latency tests.

2) SLA and uptime
- Hosted eval: no contractual SLA for eval keys; production Hosted customers on paid plans have an availability target but not the same contractual guarantees as Dedicated (which has monthly uptime SLA).

3) Quickstart & measurement guidance
- I’ve provisioned a 7-day sandbox workspace for FastStore and created an API key: FS-EVAL-xxxx-TEST (key sent in a separate secure channel).
- Quick checks: run 1000 synthetic reranking requests and report p50/p95. Use our sample script in the quickstart PDF.
- If you’d like, Marissa can join a 45-minute session to help interpret traces and tune batch sizes/kv-cache usage for reranking.

Attachments included: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (setup scripts + sample requests) and rate-limits-sla.pdf (detailed limits and migration guidance).

Next steps:

- Run the sample rerank test and share p50/p95 — we’ll follow up with recommended path (Hosted tuning vs Dedicated sizing).

Marissa — can you drop available times for a short troubleshooting session this week?
